descriptors.concept_name: Preparation of consolidated financial statements after applying above principles
descriptors.definition: The preparation of consolidated financial statements involves combining line-by-line assets, liabilities, income, expenses, and cash flows of parents and subsidiaries while eliminating intra-group transactions. It also recognizes non-controlling interests, goodwill or capital reserves, and the parent's share of post-acquisition profits.
inclusion: Combination of parent and subsidiary balance sheet, profit and loss, and cash flow items
Elimination of intra-group balances and transactions
exclusion: Unadjusted separate financial statements without elimination
nearby_distinctions: Differs from individual financial statements by incorporating group-wide entity aggregations and eliminations rather than single-entity reporting.

descriptors.definition: Chain-holding occurs when a parent company exercises indirect control over a sub-subsidiary through an intermediate subsidiary. Effective equity interest and pre-acquisition reserves are determined based on the multi-tiered ownership percentages and the specific chronological dates of acquisition.
inclusion: Determination of effective control dates for sub-subsidiaries
exclusion: Direct parent-to-subsidiary holdings without intermediary entities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from direct holdings by requiring layered percentage computations and sequential acquisition date tracking across multiple corporate levels.

descriptors.definition: Loss of control occurs when a parent ceases to hold a controlling financial interest in a subsidiary through outright sales, partial disposals, or dilutions. Upon losing control, the parent derecognizes the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, and non-controlling interests while recognizing any retained interest at fair value and recording a resulting gain or loss in profit or loss.
inclusion: Outright and partial sale of subsidiary stakes
Dilution resulting in loss of power over relevant activities
exclusion: Partial sales that do not result in a loss of control
nearby_distinctions: Differs from changes in ownership interest without loss of control, which are treated strictly as equity transactions.

descriptors.concept_name: Accounting treatment on loss of control of a subsidiary
descriptors.definition: When control is lost, the parent derecognizes the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, and non-controlling interest, and brings any retained investment onto the books at fair value. The resulting net difference is recognized as a gain or loss in profit or loss alongside reclassified amounts previously recognized in other comprehensive income.
inclusion: Fair value recognition of retained financial assets or investments in associates
Recycling of related comprehensive income components
exclusion: Transactions where control is maintained by the parent group
nearby_distinctions: Differs from intra-group reorganizations where assets remain under ultimate parent control.

descriptors.concept_name: Loss of control of a subsidiary in two or more arrangements (transactions)
descriptors.definition: Multiple disposal arrangements that result in a loss of control must be accounted for as a single transaction if they are linked contractually or economically. Criteria such as simultaneous execution, mutual interdependence, or pre-arranged pricing adjustments dictate single-transaction treatment rather than separate piecemeal disposals.
inclusion: Linked share disposals occurring in contemplation of each other
Disposals dependent on the occurrence of another arrangement
exclusion: Unrelated and economically independent sequential share sales
nearby_distinctions: Differs from isolated partial sales because combined transactions trigger profit or loss gain recognition for the entire block upon final control loss.

descriptors.concept_name: ACCOUNTING FOR A CHANGE IN INVESTMENT ENTITY STATUS
descriptors.definition: A parent entity must account for transitions into or out of investment entity status prospectively from the date of the status change. Ceasing to be an investment entity triggers the application of business combination standards using the fair value on that date as deemed consideration.
inclusion: Deemed acquisition accounting when an entity ceases to be an investment entity
exclusion: Retrospective restatement of prior periods for status changes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard acquisitions by utilizing status change dates and pre-existing fair values instead of historical cash purchase prices.

descriptors.concept_name: Accounting when an entity ceases to be an investment entity
descriptors.definition: An entity that ceases to be an investment entity treats the change date as a deemed acquisition date for its subsidiaries previously measured at fair value through profit or loss. It applies business combination principles to measure identifiable net assets, non-controlling interests, and resulting goodwill or bargain purchase gains.
terminology: Fair value through profit or loss
inclusion: Application of acquisition method to former investment entity holdings
Recognition of goodwill based on fair value consideration
exclusion: Continued fair value measurement under investment entity exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from initial corporate formations by converting investment-level fair value trackers into line-by-line consolidated assets via a deemed purchase mechanism.

descriptors.concept_name: Accounting when an entity becomes an investment entity
descriptors.definition: An entity that becomes an investment entity ceases line-by-line consolidation of its subsidiaries and applies loss-of-control accounting rules as of the change date. Any retained interest in the former subsidiaries is measured at fair value through profit or loss, with any resulting disposal gain or loss recognized immediately.
terminology: Fair value through profit or loss
inclusion: Discontinuation of consolidation for non-service subsidiaries
Measurement of retained interests at fair value on status change date
exclusion: Subsidiaries that provide investment-related services which continue to be consolidated
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard operational loss of control because the parent maintains an investment relationship categorized under specialized investment entity rules.

descriptors.concept_name: SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES BETWEEN IND AS 110 AND AS 21
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 110 mandates principle-based control definitions, strict three-month financial statement date matching limits, and mandatory consolidation exceptions, whereas AS 21 relies on quantitative voting ownership thresholds, six-month gaps, and permits certain exclusions. Furthermore, unlike AS 21, Ind AS 110 requires mandatory consolidated financial statement preparation for parents with limited exceptions.
inclusion: Reporting date interval limits between parent and subsidiary
exclusion: Identical regulatory treatment across both accounting frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts modern principle-based economic exposure models with legacy numerical voting majority thresholds and broader exclusion permissions.
